 Public speaking can be intimidating but Talking Points makes it fun! 

 Available In

 Talking Points is the fourth game for The Jackbox Party Pack 7 , where speakers are given picture slides they’ve never seen before and words to read out loud that they didn’t write. Giving a speech has never been this weird or this funny, and brings a whole 'nother meaning to "on-the-spot".

 Gameplay [ ] 

 In this game, the players take turns reading short speeches with slides that they have not seen in advance. No prep time, no context. If it's a text slide, you read it out loud. If a picture slide, you say what comes to mind. In addition, players will take turns being the Assistant to a Speaker, and choose the slides sent to the speaker. Everyone watching reacts to each of the speeches in real-time with Reactions.

 Title Creation [ ] 

 Every player fills their blanked prompts with a key point to talk about. They have three to make and three to pick from. 

 Presentation [ ] 

 After picking your title, one player presents (Speaker) and another sends them text and photos (Assistant). The Speaker has to read text they are given, and when they see a photo, they just have to say whatever comes to their minds. Everyone else reacts with Thumbs Ups or Thumbs Downs, and the Speaker gets points based on how many reactions they get.

 Presentations are structured as follows: Intro > Text > Photo > Text > Photo > Text > Photo > Closing 

 If, during a presentation, every player is at the top of the voting pole and spams the upvote button, the voting pole will extend further up, and will allow players to vote further up. The players will also be pulled back down constantly, and the pole will return to normal if people do not continue voting upwards.

 After the presentation, the Speaker gets points for the reactions, and the Assistant gets half the points listed. Other players write their comments, and the next speech begins just like before. This goes until every player gives a speech.

 Awards [ ] 

 After all people present, every player names an award they hand out to the player whose speech they loved the most. These awards give more points to the player in question, and are gifted in an Awards Ceremony.

 Free Play Mode [ ] 

 This mode can be selected manually in place of the standard game, but allows the players to have unlimited time to build and present a speech of their own choosing with text, pictures, and other sorts of strange bits.

 Characters [ ] 

 Achievements [ ] 

 Putting on a Conference 

 - Play 3 consecutive games in a row

 Name Check 

 - Give a talk with the name of one of the players in the game in the title

 Good Karma 

 - Give out the most engagements to other players but still win the game

 Long Winded 

 - Give a talk that lasts over seven minutes

 Promotional Art [ ] 

 Trivia [ ] 

 This game involves improv-style public speaking and should not be played by anyone who has glossophobia or speech anxiety. If you have either of these, play at your own risk as enjoyment may vary.

 Talking Points is a presentation party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack 7 .

 Gameplay

 Standard Play

 All players will start out by typing in a prompt in their three fill-in-the-blank titles, which three of them will be shown to other players, and they'll have to pick which one they'd want to present.

 Once all players have picked their presentation title, a queue will be set with a Speaker and an Assistant :

 The Speaker will talk out loud about their presentation, whist using their drawing and text tools to try and make the presentation that they're talking about make sense.

 The Assistant will be able to select what the next text segues and pictures should be for the Speaker to then talk about and present.

 The presentations will be presented as follows: intro, title, picture, text segue, picture, text segue, picture, outro .

 Whilst the two players are controlling the speech, the others can repeatedly click their "up" and "down" buttons on their device to interact with the speech; these buttons will contribute to the two players' presentation score.

 When the presentation's complete, two different graphs'll be shown: a point graph, detailing the amount of button presses (which are 250 points apiece), and a line graph, showing the qualitative points of the presentation (measured by if the players pressed either "up" or "down".) Both of these will add up to a total score, of which the Assistant will get half of the Speaker's score. The others can also add in a quote to be shown in the recaps, preferably detailing the presentation they've seen. The Speaker can also rate how well their Assistant during the presentation, and the Assistant will be able to pick one of the images shown as their presentation's icon.

 Once all presentations have been gone through, the almost-final scores are shown, then each player (as well as Audience members) will have one final award to give out, which they can name it whatever they want. When the award's names are in, the presentation recaps will be shown, along with a picture that the Assistant chose and the other players' quotes.

 When all of the recaps have been gone through, an Awards Ceremony will be held, and the players will all give out their awards to the player they wish, awarding the Speaker of said presentation with 75,000 bonus points. When all of the awards are given out, they're shown on-screen, as well as which player they decided to give their award to. The player who manages to earn the most points at the end of the game will win.
